claim: Iter 131 P7 per-prompt Adaptive-G* simulation on N2 reward tensors (2560 prompt cells = 4 methods × 40 steps × 16 prompts, exact observed k_p at G=8). Closed-form Bernoulli per-prompt G* rule (halve zvf_obs threshold): pick min G ∈ {8,16,32,64} s.t. zvf(G) < zvf_obs/2; refuse to escalate boundary prompts (k ∈ {0,8}, zvf(G)=1 for all G). H1 PASS — ADAPTIVE_PP mean per-step contrast_restored net of cost = +0.392 [CI: +0.167, +0.591, B=2000 seed=20260705], EXCLUDES zero (paper-grade win on per-prompt granularity, where iter-119 step-aggregate CCC could not achieve positive net). H2 PASS — G*=16 dominates G*=32 by frequency: ADAPTIVE_PP Gstar distribution {8:1867, 16:693}, NEVER G*=32 or G*=64 (closed-form zvf halves with G=16 on every N2 non-boundary prompt). H3 PASS — ADAPTIVE_PP achieves IDENTICAL contrast_magnitude to STATIC_G16 (same escalation set, same predicted zvf) at 64% of the cost: cost-equivalent efficiency ADAPTIVE_PP 0.026 contrast/unit_cost vs STATIC_G16 0.017 = 1.56x better. H4 REFUTED — per-method cost-equivalent contrast ranking is areal > aero > grpo > gift, NOT iter-127 step-aggregate CCC ranking (gift > grpo > aero > areal); the per-prompt granularity reveals a DIFFERENT method ordering that rewards low-boundary-rate methods (areal 0.7063 has the most salvageable prompts) over high-boundary-rate methods (gift 0.7703 wastes more cells on un-salvageable). Cross-paper coupling: (i) P7 iter-119 row 134 CCC unification — iter-131 is the per-prompt audit of the CCC's DEGENERATE regime at G=16 granularity (CCC said G=20.3 on N2; iter-131 confirms G=16 is sufficient at per-prompt granularity because closed-form zvf halves at G=16); (ii) P7 iter-111 row 127 ADAPTIVE-G* per-step N2 — iter-111 picked G* at step-aggregate (16 prompts lumped); iter-131 picks G* per-prompt independently (2560 decisions vs 160 step-aggregates); (iii) P7 iter-115 row 129 N10 step-aggregate — iter-115 reported ADAPTIVE-G* G=64 pessimal on step-aggregate; iter-131 confirms: per-prompt ORACLE (G=64 always) has mean net -0.20 (CI excludes 0 in negative direction), confirming step-aggregate over-allocation finding extends to per-prompt; (iv) P7 iter-127 row 140 method-axis CCC — iter-127 step-aggregate CCC ranking (gift > grpo > aero > areal) is REVERSED at per-prompt granularity (areal > aero > grpo > gift); the per-prompt ranking rewards methods with the lowest boundary_rate, the step-aggregate ranking rewards methods with the highest mean G_CCC. These two rankings measure different things and should be reported together; (v) P7 iter-103 row 121 Unified Calibrated Controller — iter-103 Pareto-frontier finding (C3 dominates C1 on contrast_magnitude/rollout) is reproduced at per-prompt granularity with even sharper separation (1.56x vs iter-103's 1.45x efficiency); (vi) Berkeley row 01 Dualformer-Auto per-prompt G — iter-131 imports the Berkeley rule as DUALFORMER_PP controller; DUALFORMER_PP has mean net -0.06 (CI includes 0), confirming the Berkeley per-prompt rule underperforms on N2 because it de-escalates too aggressively on p_hat ≥ 0.70 prompts (1723 cells drop to G=2 where zvf=1.0 is guaranteed); (vii) FRONTIER_INSIGHTS Round 2 ZVF-as-signal availability — iter-131's halve-zvf rule operationalizes the (frontier synthesis) framing that zvf is observed signal availability, not difficulty: the closed-form zvf halves as a function of G under the iid assumption, so the controller's G* choice is determined entirely by the Bernoulli inversion — there is no learning or posterior update. Operational: (a) ADOPT per-prompt ADAPTIVE_PP as the recommended P7 controller for binary-reward GRPO-family training when per-prompt zvf telemetry is available (1.56x more cost-efficient than STATIC_G16, statistically significant positive mean net); (b) REFUSE to escalate boundary prompts in any future P7 controller (the iter-131 honest policy); (c) report per-method cost-equivalent contrast ranking alongside step-aggregate CCC ranking in §4.17 — the two are complementary signals measuring different things; (d) the iter-131 G*=16 ceiling (no G*=32 or G*=64 chosen) suggests the candidate set {16,32,64} used in iter-111/115 was over-allocated at the per-prompt granularity; (e) paper-grade headline: 'per-prompt Adaptive-G* recovers +0.39 contrast per step net of cost at 64% of STATIC_G16 cost on the N2 four-method panel'.
